treats.title: Peanut Butter Pumpkin Biscuits
treats.subtitle: crunchy bone-shaped biscuits — the classic good-pup cookie
treats.dogSafe: Pure pumpkin is gentle on tummies and peanut butter is safe when it's xylitol-free. No salt or sugar added.

items.name: whole wheat flour
items.note: or oat flour for sensitive pups

items.name: pure pumpkin purée
items.note: NOT pumpkin pie filling (it has spices + sugar)
items.warn: Pie filling has nutmeg and sugar — use 100% pure pumpkin.

items.name: natural peanut butter
items.warn: Check the label: NO xylitol (also called birch sugar). Plain, unsalted is best.

items.name: water
items.note: only if the dough is dry

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.text: Stir the flour, pumpkin, eggs and peanut butter together until it forms a stiff dough. Add water 1 tbsp at a time only if it's too dry to hold together.

steps.title: Roll and cut
steps.text: Roll out on a floured counter to about 1 cm (½ in) thick. Cut into bones (or squares with a knife) and lay them on the sheet — they don't spread.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 20 minutes, flip, then bake 15–20 minutes more until firm and golden.

steps.title: Dry out for crunch
steps.text: Turn the oven off and leave the biscuits inside with the door cracked for 1 hour. Drier biscuits keep longer.

steps.title: Cool completely
steps.text: Cool on a rack before sharing or storing. Good pup!

treats.storage: Airtight jar at room temp 1 week, fridge 3 weeks, freezer 3 months.
tips: Bake them extra-dry if you want them to last longer on the counter.
Small dog? Use a tiny cutter — calories add up fast.
treats.source: Adapted from the American Kennel Club (AKC) pumpkin peanut butter dog treat recipe; ingredient safety per ASPCA Animal Poison Control.

treats.title: Frozen Yogurt Pupsicles
treats.subtitle: cool, creamy paw-shaped bites of yogurt, banana and peanut butter
treats.dogSafe: Plain yogurt and banana are dog-safe in small amounts. Pick yogurt with no sweeteners — some 'light' yogurts contain xylitol.

items.name: plain unsweetened yogurt
items.warn: Plain only — no xylitol, no artificial sweeteners, no flavours.

items.name: natural peanut butter
items.warn: Check the label: NO xylitol (also called birch sugar). Plain, unsalted is best.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Mash or blend the yogurt, banana and peanut butter until smooth.

steps.title: Fill the moulds
steps.text: Spoon into a silicone paw or ice-cube mould and tap it on the counter to settle.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Freeze at least 4 hours, until solid. Pop out and store in a freezer bag.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Give one at a time, outside or on a towel. New to dairy? Start with half a pupsicle to check Acura's tummy.

tips: Some dogs are lactose-sensitive — start small.
Swap the yogurt for pure pumpkin purée for a dairy-free version.
treats.source: Based on AKC and PetMD frozen yogurt dog treat guidance (plain, unsweetened yogurt; xylitol-free peanut butter).

treats.title: Sweet Potato Chews
treats.subtitle: slow-baked, chewy single-ingredient strips
treats.dogSafe: Plain cooked sweet potato is a healthy, fibre-rich treat. Never season it — no butter, salt, onion or garlic.

steps.title: Heat the oven low
steps.text: Heat the oven to 120°C (250°F) and line 2 baking sheets with parchment.

steps.title: Slice
steps.text: Cut the sweet potatoes lengthwise into 6 mm (¼ in) slices, then into strips. Even thickness = even drying.

steps.title: Bake low and slow
steps.text: Lay in a single layer and bake 1½ hours, then flip.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Bake 1–1½ hours more until dry and leathery (chewy) or crisp at the edges. Thinner strips finish sooner.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool completely on the sheets — they firm up as they cool.

treats.storage: Fridge in an airtight container up to 3 weeks, or freeze up to 3 months.
tips: Chewy strips are softer on older teeth; crisp ones last longer.
Supervise chewing and cut into smaller pieces for gulpers.
treats.source: Based on AKC 'sweet potato chews' guidance and PetMD notes on sweet potato for dogs (plain, cooked, unseasoned).

treats.title: Banana Oat Bites
treats.subtitle: soft, chewy 3-ingredient bites — great training rewards
treats.dogSafe: Oats and banana are dog-safe in moderation. Use plain rolled oats — never instant flavoured packets (they can have raisins or chocolate).

items.name: plain rolled oats
items.warn: Plain oats only — no flavoured or raisin packets.

items.name: natural peanut butter
items.warn: Check the label: NO xylitol (also called birch sugar). Plain, unsalted is best.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Mash the bananas, then stir in the oats, egg and peanut butter until it's a sticky dough. Let it sit 5 minutes so the oats soak.

steps.title: Scoop
steps.text: Roll tablespoons into balls, set on the sheet and press each with a fork.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 15–18 minutes until set and golden on the bottom.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool completely. Break in half for small rewards.

treats.storage: Fridge in an airtight container up to 1 week; freezer up to 3 months.
tips: Soft treats are great for training — break them into pea-size pieces.
treats.source: Adapted from AKC and Rover vet-reviewed banana oat dog treat recipes.

treats.title: Plain Chicken Jerky
treats.subtitle: one-ingredient chewy strips — high-value treat time
treats.dogSafe: Plain chicken is dog-safe. Never season it (no salt, garlic or onion) and heat it to 74°C (165°F) first so it's food-safe.

items.name: boneless skinless chicken breasts
items.note: about 600 g, partly frozen for slicing

steps.title: Slice thin
steps.text: Freeze the chicken 30 minutes, then slice with the grain into strips about 3–5 mm thick. Trim any fat.

steps.title: Make it food-safe
steps.text: Lay the strips on a parchment-lined sheet and bake at 160°C (325°F) for 10 minutes so they reach 74°C (165°F) — the USDA-recommended step before drying.

steps.title: Dry low and slow
steps.text: Lower the oven to 95°C (200°F) and bake 2–2½ hours, flipping halfway, until completely dry and they snap or bend without any moisture.

steps.title: Cool and store
steps.text: Cool completely, then store in the fridge. Wash hands, boards and counters well — raw chicken can carry salmonella.

treats.storage: Fridge in an airtight container up to 2 weeks; freezer up to 3 months.
tips: Completely dry = longer life. Any bendy, moist spots? Dry 20–30 minutes more.
Break into small pieces for training.
treats.source: Method follows USDA guidance for drying meat (heat to 74°C / 165°F before dehydrating); dog-safety per AKC homemade chicken jerky notes.

treats.title: Apple Carrot Bites
treats.subtitle: crunchy little biscuits with grated apple and carrot
treats.dogSafe: Apple (without seeds or core) and carrot are dog-safe crunchy foods. Always remove apple seeds and the core.

items.name: apple
items.warn: Remove the core and every seed — apple seeds aren't safe for dogs.

items.name: oat flour
items.note: blitz rolled oats in a blender

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (350°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Stir the grated apple, carrot and egg, then mix in the oat flour. Add water a spoonful at a time until it holds together.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Roll to 1 cm thick and cut small bones, or roll teaspoon-size balls and flatten with a fork.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 22–25 minutes until firm and lightly golden.

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Cool completely on a rack.

treats.storage: Fridge up to 1 week; freezer up to 3 months.
tips: Grate the apple and carrot finely so the bites hold together.
treats.source: Adapted from AKC and PetMD apple and carrot dog treat guidance (core and seeds removed).

never: in some peanut butters, sugar-free gum, candy, baked goods — even a little can be deadly
raw, cooked or powdered — damage red blood cells
no salt, butter or spice mixes on treats
watch out for pumpkin pie filling
rules: Treats should be under 10% of Acura's daily calories — the other 90% is regular food.
New food? Start with a small piece and watch for tummy upset for 24 hours.
Ask your vet before adding treats if Acura has allergies, a sensitive stomach, diabetes or kidney issues.
Always have fresh water out — and supervise chewing.
safety.emergency: Ate something dangerous? Call your vet or the ASPCA Animal Poison Control Center (1-888-426-4435, fee may apply) right away.
safety.source: ASPCA Animal Poison Control 'People Foods to Avoid Feeding Your Pets'; AKC; WSAVA calorie guidance.
